narrative.overview: The home is not a landing page; it is the screen a futures trader stares at. Its whole argument — we execute the rules competitors merely describe — is carried by one dense, aligned, scannable table of real accounts, dropped straight under a tight masthead. The mood is instrument-panel, not marketing: a flat near-black violet-tinted ground (#070510), 1px hairline rules instead of boxes, monospace column headers, and numbers that hold their column. Depth is almost entirely refused on data surfaces. The one warmth in the room is the indigo→fuchsia brand gradient, and it is spent on exactly one block per page. The palette makes the product's honesty POV visible: risk states (lime/amber/red) do the talking on every rule cell, and the brand accent is forbidden from ever carrying a data value. Confirmed anti-references: pastel rounded fintech; the competitor marketing card-grid; and any blue/cyan, banned outright. Glass and relief are not rejected — they are the product's navigation and app language — but kept off the home's data.
keyCharacteristics: Flat near-black ground; structure drawn with 1px hairlines, never cards or shadows, on data.
One brand gradient fill per page; everything else that reads as 'signal' is a risk state color.
Monospace only for measurement (column heads, grid figures, status readouts); Sora display, Inter body.
Risk semantics (lime/amber/red) own every rule cell; the brand accent never touches data.
One authored motion: a capped, staggered row cascade — content fully visible without it.

rules.name: The No-Accent-On-Data Rule
rules.body: The indigo/fuchsia brand accent may mark a control or an active/emphasis state, but never encodes the value of a datum. Every informational color on a data cell is lime, amber, or red.

rules.name: The Muted-Scan Floor
rules.body: Small text meant to be read as information uses Muted Scan (#9a8cbe), not Ink-3. Ink-3 is furniture only; if it labels a column or names a plan, it clears AA.

rules.name: The Mono-Measures-Only Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is confined to measurement chrome and grid figures on this terminal surface — a scoped reopening of the product-wide 'mono rejected for data numbers' decision, for the home grid alone. Everywhere else, data numbers stay Inter tabular.

rules.name: The Tabular-Number Rule
rules.body: Every figure compared down a column is tabular (mono .tnum on the grid, Inter .num elsewhere) so digits hold width and columns never jitter.

rules.name: The Flat-Data Rule
rules.body: Data surfaces carry no drop shadow, no backdrop-filter, no card chrome; structure is hairlines and tint. This is the home's boundary against the product's relief/glass system, which is legitimate on the floating nav layer — do not import it onto the terminal, and do not ban glass product-wide.

dos: Do keep data surfaces flat: hairlines and tint washes for structure, never cards or shadows on the table, rows, or readout.
Do spend exactly one gradient fill per page, on the payout block; make every other signal a lime/amber/red state.
Do use lime/amber/red for every rule/state cell (TRAIL=amber, funded hardening=red, unchanged/verified/no-consistency=lime, present-consistency=amber).
Do set grid figures and measurement chrome in JetBrains Mono .tnum; all other data numbers in Inter tabular .num; body and headings in Inter/Sora.
Do use Muted Scan (#9a8cbe) for small scannable text; reserve Ink-3 for furniture.
Do gate the row cascade behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and cap the stagger (~13ms x up to 26 rows); content fully visible without it.
Do stack the table into labeled per-offer cards below 860px; scroll it inside its own box (with the hint) between 861-1320px.
Do keep whole rows as real links with composed aria-labels and the visual header row aria-hidden.
donts: Don't use the brand accent (indigo/fuchsia/magenta) to encode a data value — accent marks attention or an active control, never meaning.
Don't use any blue or cyan, anywhere. The direction is tested and rejected.
Don't add a second gradient, or make the top-row rail a gradient — it is a solid fuchsia.
Don't put glass or directional-relief on the home's data; that language belongs to the product's floating nav layer — but don't ban glass across the product either.
Don't render the table as a <table> or let it scroll the page; it is a grid of links that scrolls only inside its own box.
Don't pulse the live dot or fake a stream — the dot is static because the data is dated, not real-time.
Don't promote Ink-3 to carry small informational text on the near-black ground (it fails AA); use Muted Scan.
